text: Potato late blight attacks leaves, stems and tubers. On leaves it begins as pale green, water-soaked, irregular patches near the tip and edges that grow into large brown to purplish-black dead areas. In humid weather a white mildew can be seen on the underside of the leaf. Lesions on stems and leaf stalks make them weak and they may collapse. In favourable weather the whole crop can look blighted and be destroyed within about a week.

source.document: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute, Indian Farming 74(5), May 2024, pages 52 to 58: Disease management in seed potato production

text: Late blight is caused by the water mould Phytophthora infestans. It spreads and builds up fastest at moderate temperatures of about 15 to 20 degrees Celsius and relative humidity above 80 percent. Tubers in the soil are infected by spores washed down from diseased leaves, and affected tubers show reddish brown to purplish patches that extend inside.

source.document: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute, Indian Farming 74(5), May 2024, pages 52 to 58: Disease management in seed potato production

text: To lower the risk of late blight, plant certified healthy seed tubers and do not cut them, use resistant varieties where available, and clear weeds and crop remains from the field. Deep ploughing twice during peak summer or winter helps reduce carry-over of the pathogen. Rotations of three or more years between potato crops reduce early infection, because resting spores can survive up to three years in crop remains in the soil.

source.document: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute, Indian Farming 74(5), May 2024, pages 52 to 58: Disease management in seed potato production

text: Potato early blight shows as small, dark brown to black, dry, papery spots on leaves, often angular because the veins limit them. Larger spots can have concentric rings like a target, and the leaf tissue around them often turns yellow. Spots may join together and make the field look blighted. On tubers the lesions are dark, sunken and shallow.

source.document: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute, Indian Farming 74(5), May 2024, pages 52 to 58: Disease management in seed potato production

text: Early blight is caused by Alternaria fungi, mainly Alternaria solani. Warm, humid weather of about 24 to 29 degrees Celsius and alternating wet and dry spells favour its spread. The fungus carries over from season to season on volunteer potato and tomato plants and on weedy plants of the same family.

source.document: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute, Indian Farming 74(5), May 2024, pages 52 to 58: Disease management in seed potato production

text: Use disease-free seed tubers for planting. Remove and destroy infected plant remains, because spores and fungal threads in the soil and debris are the main source of the next infection and can stay alive for more than a year. Spores are carried to nearby plants by wind, rain and insects. A variety with fair resistance, such as Kufri Sindhuri, also helps.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Horticultural crops, Vegetables, Potato: early blight

text: Tomato early blight causes brown spots with concentric rings in a bull's eye pattern, often with a yellow edge. Fruits can be infected through the calyx or stem end and show brown concentric rings. Warm, humid, rainy weather of about 24 to 29 degrees Celsius favours the disease.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Tomato diseases: early blight, updated June 2023

text: The early blight fungus survives in infected plant debris, can spread through infected seed, and then moves by rain and wind. Remove and destroy crop debris, rotate crops, and treat seed with Trichoderma asperellum before sowing as directed on the product label.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Tomato diseases: early blight, updated June 2023

text: Rice blast attacks the leaves, leaf collar, stem nodes, neck and panicle. Leaf spots start as small specks that grow into spindle-shaped spots with a grey or ash-coloured centre and a brown border. Nodes can turn black and break. Severe attacks give the field a burnt look and can lodge the crop after ear emergence.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, expert system for paddy: blast

text: Rice blast is caused by the fungus Magnaporthe oryzae and can infect leaves, neck, nodes and seed at any growth stage. It is favoured by temperatures of about 22 to 28 degrees Celsius, relative humidity above 95 percent, dew, leaf wetness for more than 10 hours, heavy nitrogen use and aerobic soils. Leaf and neck infections are the most severe.

source.document: Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage, advisory on blast disease of rice dated 22.07.2022

text: Keep the field clean and remove infected seed, panicles and plant debris after harvest. Rotate with non-host crops, use certified disease-free seed, and keep the paddy at the recommended water level, since blast is worse where the water falls below it. Remove and burn diseased plant parts. Seed and seedling treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens protects against seed and soil borne disease.

source.document: Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage, advisory on blast disease of rice dated 22.07.2022

text: Grape downy mildew is caused by Plasmopara viticola. Infected leaves show yellowish, oil-like spots on the upper surface.

source.document: Plant Archives 26(1), 2026, pages 793 to 800: Management of downy mildew (Plasmopara viticola) in grapevine using non-systemic fungicides

text: Downy mildew of grape occurs in warm, wet and humid weather and affects all commercial grape varieties in Maharashtra.

source.document: Indian Journal of Horticulture 67(4), December 2010, pages 425 to 432: Crop loss in grapes due to downy mildew infection on clusters at pre- and post bloom stages

text: Brown plant hopper nymphs and adults gather at the base of the rice plant just above the water level and suck sap. The affected plants dry up in circular patches called hopper burn, and mature plants may lodge. The insect leaves honeydew that causes sooty mould at the base and spreads grassy stunt, ragged stunt and wilted stunt diseases.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Crop Protection, Pest of paddy: brown plant hopper

text: Check the base of the tillers regularly. The action level is about 1 hopper per tiller when there are no predatory spiders, and about 2 hoppers per tiller when spiders are present at about 1 per hill. Avoid close planting and control irrigation by alternate wetting and drying.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Crop Protection, Pest of paddy: brown plant hopper

text: Keep bunds and fields free of weeds that shelter the hopper, and plant neighbouring fields within three weeks of each other with a rice-free period in between. Where the infestation is heavy, drain the field for at least 3 to 4 days, avoid excess nitrogen, and split nitrogen along with potassium. Protect natural enemies such as egg parasitoids, spiders, beetles and the mirid bug Cyrtorhinus lividipennis.

source.document: Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage, advisory on Brown Plant Hopper of rice dated July 2022

text: Neem oil mixed with a little liquid detergent, or neem seed kernel extract, can reduce egg laying and can be used when the infestation is below the action level. Direct sprays at the base of the plants. Use any pesticide only as per its registered label.

source.document: Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage, advisory on Brown Plant Hopper of rice dated July 2022

text: The rice leaf roller, also called leaf folder, is a caterpillar that folds leaves lengthways and feeds inside. It scrapes the green tissue so the leaf turns white and dry, and in severe attacks the whole field looks scorched.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Crop Protection, Pest of paddy: leaf folder or leaf roller

text: The action level is about 10 percent leaf damage in the vegetative stage and 5 percent damage on the flag leaf at flowering. Avoid too much nitrogen fertiliser, keep the bunds clean, release the egg parasitoid Trichogramma chilonis at about 30, 37 and 44 days after planting, and use neem seed kernel extract or a neem-based spray.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Crop Protection, Pest of paddy: leaf folder or leaf roller

text: Yellow stem borer moths lay brown egg masses near the leaf tip. The caterpillar bores into the central shoot of seedlings and tillers and dries it, which is called dead heart. In older plants the whole panicle dries and turns white, which is called white ear. Affected shoots pull out easily by hand.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Crop Protection, Pest of rice: paddy stemborer

text: When egg masses reach the action level of about 2 per square metre, release the egg parasitoid Trichogramma japonicum. A spray of neem seed kernel extract also helps control stem borer.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Crop Protection, Pest of rice: paddy stemborer

text: Clip and remove affected leaves, keep the bunds clean and grow resistant varieties where they are available.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Srinivasan and Kishan Tej, Insect Pests of Field Crops and their Management, pests of paddy

text: Aphids are small sap-sucking insects found on young leaves, shoots, stems, flowers and pods. Heavy feeding twists the young leaves and causes yellowing and wilting, and the honeydew they leave attracts sooty mould. Some aphid species also spread plant viruses.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Crop Protection, Pests of Black and Green Gram: bean aphids

text: Yellow sticky traps help reduce and monitor aphid numbers. Ladybird beetles and green lacewings are efficient natural enemies of aphids, so avoid harming them. A spray of crude neem extract or neem oil is a gentle first option.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Crop Protection, Pests of Black and Green Gram: bean aphids

text: Avoid late sowing and apply nitrogen fertiliser judiciously. Growing cowpea as an intercrop or on the bunds helps natural enemies build up. For cotton the action level is about 15 percent of plants infested, so check the local action level for your crop before spraying.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Crop Protection, Pest of Cotton: cotton aphid

text: Thrips nymphs and adults scrape the leaf and suck the sap that oozes out, leaving white patches on the underside of the leaves, and severe attacks turn leaves bronze. Nymphs are yellow and adults are black with fringed wings. Some thrips species spread viruses such as peanut bud necrosis virus.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Crop Production Entomology, Groundnut: thrips

text: Keep the field clean and remove weeds that harbour thrips and the viruses they spread. Yellow or blue sticky traps can be used to monitor and mass trap thrips.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Crop Protection, Chrysanthemum: thrips management

text: Scirtothrips dorsalis is a thrips. Thrips nymphs and adults scrape the leaf and suck the sap that oozes out, leaving white patches on the underside of the leaves, and severe attacks turn leaves bronze. Nymphs are yellow and adults are black with fringed wings. Some thrips species spread viruses such as peanut bud necrosis virus.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Crop Production Entomology, Groundnut: thrips

text: To manage Scirtothrips dorsalis and other thrips: keep the field clean and remove weeds that harbour thrips and the viruses they spread. Yellow or blue sticky traps can be used to monitor and mass trap thrips.

source.document: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Agritech Portal, Crop Protection, Chrysanthemum: thrips management
